question: Will Turkey's NDK have issued an operating license for Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 by September 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: NDK's licensing page shows Unit 1's operating-licence application only reached the 'review and evaluation' stage after supplementary documents were filed 1 June 2026 — no board decision, and no public signal that review is complete. Physically the unit is not there either: turbine-hall commissioning (condenser vacuum, then turbogenerator gas-tightness) was still running as of 6 Aug 2026, and the most recent reporting (3 Sep 2026) frames real fuel loading — which the licence must precede — as 'end of September or beginning of October' at best. With ~10 days left in the window and issuance plausibly spread across a 75-90 day autumn, uniform continuation gives ~11%; Akkuyu's consistent one-directional slippage and the first-of-a-kind nature of Turkey's first operating licence pull that down, while weekly-ish NDK board cadence, the December mandatory deadline, and post-Bishkek political pressure keep it off the floor. Beware the near-miss: Unit 2's decision 2026-13/1 was a commissioning permit, and much reporting mislabels it 'operating permission' — that does not resolve this YES. No prediction market on any venue prices this event.
calls.reference_class: Announced-but-undated national regulatory approvals for first-of-a-kind nuclear milestones, evaluated over a 10-day slice of a ~3-month expected issuance window, in projects with a documented history of schedule slippage
